newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Westpac -BML merger to win approval -paper.
newsitem.headline: Westpac -BML merger to win approval -paper.

text.p: Westpac Banking Corp Ltd's A$1.4 billion bid to merge with Bank of Melbourne Ltd is likely to be granted conditional approval by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC), The Australian Financial Review newspaper said on Wednesday.
"Sources close to talks between Westpac and the ACCC say the deal will go ahead, with the final negotiations hingeing on the details of the merger," the Financial Review said.
The ACCC has said it expected to announce a decision on the merger later this week, possibly as early as later on Wednesday.

The Financial Review quoted one source as saying: "We think we can be confident that this will proceed. But it is in the nature of these conditions that working out how they will be put into place is not straightforward -- that may take a few more days."
In April, Westpac offered A$9.75 a share for the Bank of Melbourne, valuing the regional bank at about A$1.435 billion.
Westpac's shares closed down 12 cents at A$7.80, while Bank of Melbourne's shares closed up five cents at A$9.45.
The A$9.75 a share bid includes a 90 cent per share fully franked special dividend and the balance of A$8.85 can be paid either completely in cash or as one Westpac share and up to A$1.85 in cash.
